intro.title: Test useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for a custom React hook called `useFetch` that fetches data from an API. You'll learn how to write unit tests using React Testing Library and Jest to verify that the hook correctly handles loading states, successful data returns, and error scenarios. The core programming concept involves mocking HTTP requests with tools like `jest.mock` or `fetch.mock` to simulate different API responses without making real network calls. You'll work with React hooks, asynchronous testing patterns, and assertion methods to ensure your custom hook behaves as expected under various conditions.
intro.usecase: Testing custom hooks like useFetch is a critical skill for ensuring data reliability in production React applications. Developers must verify that components fetching user profiles, dashboard metrics, or product listings handle loading, error, and success states correctly. For example, in an e-commerce admin panel, robust tests for a useFetch hook powering order history or inventory data prevent UI crashes and provide a seamless user experience. This practice ensures your application remains stable and responsive when integrating with real APIs.
